newsitem.title: UK: Briton convicted after bogus miracle cure.
newsitem.headline: Briton convicted after bogus miracle cure.

text.p: A British man who pretended he was crippled and then staged a miraculous cure was jailed for 21 months on Monday after being convicted of conspiracy to defraud.

It took a jury in Birmingham Crown Court just over an hour to convict Paul Redhead, 29, who rose from his wheelchair in a Pentecostal church in Coventry, northern England, after accepting money from parishioners to buy a new wheelchair.
"The devout congregation believed they were witnessing a miracle and there was great excitement," said prosecutor David Iles.
Redhead proclaimed it was a miracle and that God had cured him, but when doubting church ministers asked for medical proof he produced bogus documents.

Redhead and a friend, who was sentenced to 15 months in jail, dreamed up the scam after he was temporarily confined to a wheelchair in 1995 after suffering ill effects from drugs he had been taking for epilepsy.
Neighbours and church members raised 500 pounds ($800) for a new wheelchair after the pair said money they had saved for a chair had been stolen.
